content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory-to-Sales Acceleration", "construction": "Compute the year-over-year change in the ratio of inventories (Compustat item INVT) to sales (SALE), then take the second difference (acceleration) across two consecutive fiscal years. Rank cross-sectionally each June using the most recent annual data.", "rationale": "Accelerating inventory buildup relative to sales signals unanticipated demand weakness and future margin pressure that the market is slow to price.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (decelerating inventory relative to sales)"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Growth Deflated by Assets", "construction": "Use reported order backlog (Compustat item OB) scaled by total assets (AT), measured as the year-over-year change. Rank firms each June; restrict to firms that report nonzero backlog.", "rationale": "Growing backlog reflects strong committed future demand not yet in earnings, and investors underreact to this forward-looking soft signal.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (rising backlog-to-assets)"}, {"name": "Employee Productivity Momentum", "construction": "Compute sales per employee (SALE / EMP) and take the two-year growth rate. Rank cross-sectionally each June using annual Compustat data.", "rationale": "Rising revenue per worker signals operating efficiency gains and restructuring benefits that translate into future profitability improvements underappreciated by the market.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"}, {"name": "Dispersion Between Cash and Accrual Earnings Trends", "construction": "For each firm compute the 3-year trend (slope of regression on time) in cash flow from operations scaled by assets and separately the trend in total accruals scaled by assets. Take the difference (cash trend minus accrual trend). Rank each June.", "rationale": "Firms whose cash-based earnings are strengthening while accruals shrink have higher-quality, more persistent earnings that the market undervalues.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (cash improving relative to accruals)"}, {"name": "Volume-Weighted Price Range Compression", "construction": "For each stock compute the average daily high-low range (from CRSP daily data) divided by closing price over the prior 3 months, then compute its change relative to the range over the prior 12 months. Rank monthly.", "rationale": "Compressing intraday ranges indicate declining uncertainty and information resolution, preceding positive drift as risk premia normalize downward.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (compressing range)"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Deviation from Industry Norm", "construction": "Compute capex (CAPX) scaled by lagged assets, subtract the contemporaneous industry (2-digit SIC) median, and rank the firm-specific deviation each June.", "rationale": "Firms investing far above industry norms tend to over-invest and destroy value, generating lower subsequent returns due to overextrapolation of growth.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (below-industry capex)"}, {"name": "Financing Gap Indicator", "construction": "Compute the ratio of (capital expenditures + dividends + change in working capital minus operating cash flow) to total assets, a measure of external financing need. Rank firms each June.", "rationale": "Firms with a large internal financing shortfall must access capital markets and face higher scrutiny and dilution risk, producing lower future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (self-financing firms)"}, {"name": "Return-on-Assets Stability", "construction": "Compute the standard deviation of quarterly ROA (net income / total assets, from Compustat quarterly) over the trailing 12 quarters, inverted so that stable firms score high. Rank each quarter.", "rationale": "Stable operating profitability signals durable competitive advantage and lower cash-flow risk that investors underprice relative to volatile-earnings firms.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (stable ROA)"}, {"name": "Tax-Book Income Divergence", "construction": "Estimate taxable income from the current tax expense (TXT minus deferred tax TXDI) divided by the statutory rate, and compare to pretax book income (PI). Compute the ratio of estimated taxable income to book income; rank each June.", "rationale": "When taxable income is high relative to book income, book earnings are less likely inflated by discretionary accruals, indicating higher earnings quality and future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (taxable income high relative to book)"}, {"name": "Turnover-Adjusted Reversal", "construction": "Compute the prior 1-month stock return and interact its sign with abnormal share turnover (monthly volume/shares outstanding relative to its own 12-month average) using CRSP data. Short recent winners with abnormally high turnover and buy recent losers with abnormally low turnover; rank the composite.", "rationale": "Short-term reversal is stronger among stocks with liquidity-driven, high-turnover price moves, which reflect temporary price pressure rather than information.", "higher_returns_for": "low prior return combined with low abnormal turnover (past losers with quiet volume)"}]}
